And all who were present there answered, saying: “Let it be done, let it be done.”

The names of some of them are written here, namely, first:

Martin, bishop of the holy Church of Sutrium. Wido, bishop of the holy Church of Sersina. John, bishop of the holy Church of Cornelium. Azio, chief notary and apocrisiarius of the holy Roman Church. John, duke of the city of Rome, who is called Gambaruto. Stephen, *iniculator* of the city of Rome [the title is uncertain]. Also Paul, glorious judge. Vigo, judge of Ferrara. Peter, *dativus* of this city of Ravenna [an official title]. John, *dativus* of Ferrara. Leo, *dativus* from the city of Faenza. Peter and Stephen, *dativi* of Ferrara. Count Peter. Garardus and Hirardus, of the counts. Arderatus and Rambertus, brothers and counts. John, duke of Romano. John and Almericus, his brothers and sons. Paul and Peter, dukes of Traversaria. Peter, son of that Paul. Duke Romuald. Paul, son of Vitabianus. John, consul and patrician. Heraldus, son of Jaraldus, from the ducal lineage. Atelbertus and Sergius, brothers and dukes. Andrew, son of the late Amabilis, *dativus*. Deusdedit of Ponte Augusto. Gasirius, son of John the consul. Vitalis of Liuto. John and Luicio, brothers, sons of the late Anastasius the consul. Leotarius. Peter of Malo. Mauritius Spaza Inferno [the name or epithet is uncertain]. Vitalis, son of Vitalis of Marino.

As for the notaries, the citizens of Ravenna:

John, consul among the notaries, who is called Uter. Stephen, notary. Dominic, notary. Apollinaris, notary. Sergius, notary.

As for the chancellors:

Vitalis, chancellor. Martin, chancellor and *sarsor* [the office is uncertain]. Leo, chancellor. Sarius of Cisterno. Dominic and Bernard, chancellors of the Gaudentian tree. All these were from the city of Ravenna.

As for the men of Ferrara: John, archpriest of the holy Ferrara Church. Lopicinus, archdeacon. Peter the priest, George the priest, Bonizo the priest and *primicerius*, and John, archisubdeacon.

As for the laymen:

Leo of Andrea, consul. Refredo, his son; Leo, consul. Gregory of Daniel. Another Gregory, consul. Peter, consul, son of Leo the consul. Anselm, consul, son of Raimbald. Paul, consul, who is called of Nastasia. John, who is called of Cristinia; and a multitude of other men whose names would be too lengthy to write.

## V. Bull of Pope John XIII to Gerberga, Abbess of Gandersheim (968)

At the request of Otto the Elder and Otto the Younger, he undertakes the protection of the Gandersheim nunnery and confirms its possessions and rights.

[According to Mansi, *Councils*, vol. XVIII, col. 529.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to Gerberga, resplendent in merit and nobility of blood, our most beloved daughter in Christ, venerable abbess of the monastery of the holy confessors Innocent and Anastasius, which is called Gandersheim, and to her successors, perpetual salvation and apostolic blessing.

If we grant assent to pious vows and petitions, we believe that we please almighty God. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the sons of the holy Catholic Church, present and future, that at the synod held at the body of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, in the month of December and in the eleventh indiction, our beloved and spiritual sons, Otto the Elder and Otto the Younger, most serene emperors Augustus, humbly entreated our apostolic fatherhood before thirty-six archbishops and bishops, both Italian and transalpine, that we should fortify by the protection of our authority the aforesaid monastery of Gandersheim, which is situated under the governance of your daughterhood in the kingdom of Lower Saxony, in honor of the aforesaid confessors of Christ, Innocent and Anastasius, and that we should perpetually receive it under the protection and jurisdiction of the holy apostolic See.

Rejoicing wholeheartedly in their pious petitions, we have decreed that this be done, commanding by that authority with which we are supported in the office of keeper of the heavenly kingdom that no secular person should ever possess the aforesaid venerable monastery, nor should anyone appropriate anything from its tithes or possessions—not a king, margrave, count, bishop, or any prince endowed with whatever power—unless perhaps for the purpose of protecting and defending it, and then only with the sober permission of yourself and of whichever abbess is regularly in office at the time.

Be, therefore, abbess of that monastery for the praise of the almighty King, and do not cease, by wise instruction, to urge the sisters subject to you to seek the joys of the heavenly homeland. Let those sisters always have the power and permission, after the death of the abbess, to substitute for themselves another mother from their own congregation according to their rule; and let them have the power to elect, with equal disposition and consent, whomever they judge more worthy.

We confirm and strengthen for that holy monastery all the movable and immovable goods and possessions which it now has and which, with God’s help, it ought henceforth to have by any lawful mode of acquisition, so that from now and forever it may freely hold and possess them, with every human contradiction removed.

But if anyone should attempt to act against the protection of this our apostolic privilege, and should endeavor to overturn anything decreed by us, we excommunicate that person with the help of the holy and undivided Trinity and through the intercession of blessed Mary ever-virgin and all the saints, by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, with the consent of the provincial bishops and all the suffragan bishops of this our holy See; and we perpetually anathematize that person, separating them from the thresholds of the holy Church of God and from the fellowship of all Christians.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary of the holy Roman Church, in the aforesaid month and eleventh indiction. Farewell. Given on the Kalends of January by the hand of Wido, bishop of the holy Church of Silva Candida and librarian of the holy apostolic See, in the third year, by God’s favor, of the pontificate of Lord John, supreme pontiff and universal pope, the thirteenth of that name, in the most holy See of the apostle blessed Peter; under the most serene emperors, Lords Otto the Elder and Otto the Younger; in the sixth year of the Elder’s empire and the first of the Younger’s, in the month and eleventh indiction.

## VI. Bull of Pope John XIII for the Monastery of Saint Maximinus at Trier (968)

[According to Mansi, cited above, col. 531.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable abbot, our beloved son in Christ, Theitfrid, apostolic blessing and greeting.

It is fitting for apostolic governance to assist with benevolent compassion those distinguished by pious religion and to grant with joyful devotion the assent requested by their hearts; for by this we undoubtedly earn the greatest reward from God, the creator of all, when venerable places, suitably ordered, have been restored to a better condition.

Since, therefore, your religious devotion asks that we grant to your monastery—which is known to have been built in the suburb of Trier in honor of the most blessed confessor of Christ, Maximinus—the privilege of our holy apostolic Church, over which by God’s authority we preside, in order to preserve for you, your brothers, and your successors the norm of monastic tranquility, we have taken care to grant your petition our favorable assent.

By a decree of apostolic authority, therefore, we determine that the congregation serving God and Saint Maximinus religiously shall henceforth have the free power, just as it was granted by our beloved son Otto and by the other kings and emperors of the Franks, to create from among themselves whomever they choose before God as their abbot. No person of any rank may presume to arrange or rashly exercise anything within the monastery according to his own will, unless summoned by you or by another abbot who succeeds you.

Furthermore, by our apostolic authority we absolutely forbid that it ever be subjected to any church or see by exchange or by any other transaction; rather, with such liberty and immunity as the monastery of Prüm and the other royal places enjoy, let it always remain unharmed and perpetual.

We command by apostolic decree that the monastery itself remain perpetually under the protection of kings or emperors, the sons, namely, of the holy Roman Church. It shall never be open to any person as a benefice or for seizure, but shall gladly remain, without anyone’s contradiction, for the use and tranquility of the monks serving God there under the rule of Saint Benedict.

To increase and complete monastic tranquility, we add that no person of any rank may presume to alienate or diminish anything, even the smallest thing, from the church’s possessions, whether from those now bestowed upon your monastery or from those which other faithful people shall bestow day by day.

But if anyone—God forbid—should presume with wicked audacity to violate or in any way infringe what we have established for the praise of almighty God and the stability of the aforesaid venerable monastery, we bind that person inseparably with the bond of anathema by the authority of almighty God, through the intercession of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, whose office we hold, and by the apostolic constitution of our humanity, with the consent of all the provincial and suffragan bishops.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary of the holy Roman Church. Read in the synod held at Rome, with the divine emperors Otto the Great and his namesake son seated in attendance, in the sixth year of the Elder’s empire and the first of the Younger’s. Given on the fourth day before the Nones of January.

## VII. Bull of Pope John XIII for the Monastery of Blessed John the Evangelist at Meissen (968)

[According to Mansi, cited above, col. 532.]

If those things which accord with pious desires are always to be granted, then all the more must those things which are recognized as pertaining to the prerogative of divine worship not be abolished altogether; such things are not only to be requested from their benefactors but, by the force of charity, unquestionably to be demanded.

Accordingly, after a synod had been held and a gathering of many venerable fathers and our fellow bishops had assembled at Rome in the church of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, with both most august emperors Otto seated in attendance—in the sixth year of the Elder’s empire and the first of the Younger’s—the same most glorious emperors asked us to adorn with the privileges of the apostolic See the monastery which they had first caused to be built for the remedy of their souls and consecrated in honor of blessed John the Evangelist, on the bank of the river called the Elbe, in the city of Meissen, situated in the province called Daleminzia, and over which they had honorably placed a venerable man named Burchard.

They asked that, since it had been established under the jurisdiction of our holy Church, over which by God’s authority we preside, it should not be subjected to the dominion of any other church. Favoring their pious desires, by this authority of ours we put what they request into effect, while also inserting those matters which our princes themselves wish to be set forth through numerous privileges and made known to all the faithful in Christ.

Following the custom of the ancient emperors, these two emperors, father and son, seated with us, established the boundary of the bishopric of Meissen by naming the limits and boundaries of the places, as follows:

Where there is the head and source of the water called the Oder; from there, as though by a straight road, to the head of the Elbe; from there downstream toward the west, where the division of the two regions of Bohemia and Nisani is found. From there beyond the Elbe, and through the forest toward the west, as far as the head of the Mulde; and then downstream along both banks of that same river, until the Mulde enters the Elbe. We have specified the western bank because many villages belong to the eastern towns below the same boundary. Then upward and beyond the province of the Nizizi, to that same boundary without doubt.

Likewise, on the other side, through Lusatia and Selpuli, and so as far as the city of Sulpice—that is, the part of it lying within the same boundary—and from there to the water called the Oder; and then upstream along the Oder as far as its head.

All those who, as the emperors presently in attendance acknowledge, live within this boundary shall pay, render, and return to the Church of Meissen, first to God and then to Saint John the Evangelist, without any uncertainty whatsoever, the tithes which they owe to God, who governs all things: from every fertility of the land, crops, and livestock; in silver and clothing; and also in what the Germans call *Ubercota* [Note: See Du Cange, *Glossary*, under “Ouercoupunga.”] and *Telunga* of households; in addition, from every benefit and from all things used by mortals, in their various forms of tithing.

The same noble emperors presently in attendance also testify that they have given as property certain things belonging to their own right and ownership to the same holy Church of Meissen, over which the venerable Bishop Burchard is known to preside, for the remedy of their souls. Namely, from their tributes in five regions, a tenth share: in Daleminzia, in Nisa, in Milzane, in Lusatia, and in Diedesa. Before the count of those regions takes away and distributes the portion granted to him by them, he shall pay the tithes in full and entirety to the aforesaid holy Church of God: namely in honey, *crusina* [Note: A kind of fur garment. Du Cange, s.v. “Crusna.”], payment in silver, slaves, clothing, pigs, grain, and all things that appear to belong to the treasury of the aforesaid emperors.

They have also established that the holy Church of Meissen, and Saint John the Evangelist, shall possess as their own the toll from the city called Belgern as far as the port of the same Church of Meissen upstream, and from there again along both banks of the aforesaid river Elbe downstream; and wherever, within the prescribed boundary, the hands of merchants turn this way or that across the Elbe, the toll shall be paid and delivered in full and without any contradiction to the aforesaid See of Meissen perpetually.

Therefore, in Christ we have firmly sanctioned and granted that no metropolitan, no bishop, and no person of any other order or rank, great or small, except the bishop of the apostolic See, may presume in any way within the boundaries of the Church of Meissen, over which the venerable Bishop Burchard is known to preside, to ordain, judge, excommunicate, or rashly exercise any authority over anyone.

We further establish by apostolic censure, under adjuration by the divine judgment and by strong and terrible prohibitions of anathema, that no emperor thereafter, no king, nor anyone else endowed with power of whatever rank, may presume to interfere in the affairs of that Church, or to seize for himself even the smallest thing that appears to belong to the monastery of Saint John, over which Bishop Burchard presides, or to give it as a benefice to any person, great or small, or in any way dare to remove or alienate it.

We also promulgate, and by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, before God and his terrible future judgment, we threaten through the force of this privilege and constitution that no mortal should presume himself permitted to take anything from the possessions of the Church of Meissen—whether from those previously offered and bestowed upon that holy place by the glorious emperors Otto and his namesake son, or by other Christians, or from those which are to be bestowed later—so that, in accordance with what follows, that venerable place may remain securely endowed by this apostolic privilege.

But if anyone—something we emphatically do not desire—should presume by wicked authority to oppose what we have established for the praise of God and the stability of the aforesaid monastery, and should become a transgressor of our decree, let that person know that he is bound by the bond of anathema and assigned, together with the devil and Judas the betrayer of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the punishment of eternal fire.

But whoever, with pious regard, proves himself an observer of this apostolic constitution shall receive manifoldly the grace of blessing from the most merciful Lord God and may deserve to become a participant in eternal life.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary of the holy Roman Church, in the month of December, in the eleventh indiction.

Sign of Lord Otto the Younger, emperor Augustus.

Peter, archbishop of the Church of Ravenna, subscribed. Rodaldus, patriarch of Aquileia, subscribed. Sigolfus, bishop of the holy Church of Piacenza, consented and subscribed. Udalricus, bishop of the holy Church of Bergamo, consented and subscribed. Siggo, bishop of the Church of Pledensis [Blerensis], consented and subscribed. Benedict, bishop of the holy Church of Fulginia, consented and subscribed. John, bishop of the holy Church of Narni [Note: “Narniensis.” But below there is Stephen of Narni], subscribed. John, bishop of the holy Church of Gallia, subscribed. John, bishop of the holy Church of Ariminum [Rimini], was present and subscribed. Humbert, bishop of the holy Church of Luna, consented and subscribed. Gerhard, bishop of the Church of Faenza, consented and subscribed. Aufredus [Wigfredus], bishop of the Church of Verdun, consented and subscribed. Zenobius, bishop of the Church of Fiesole, consented and subscribed. Gaidolfus, bishop of the Church of Fermo, consented and subscribed. I, Peter, bishop of the Church of Camerino, was there and subscribed. Eberhardus, bishop of Arezzo, consented and subscribed. Stephen, bishop of the Church of Narni, consented and subscribed. Alberinus, bishop of Ascoli, subscribed. Antonius, bishop of the Church of Brescia [Note: “Brixiensis” is the correct reading, since Labbe has “Brisunensis”], subscribed. Diotericus, bishop of the Church of Metz, subscribed. Lanwardus, bishop of Minden, subscribed. Huibertus, bishop, subscribed. Luzo, bishop of Cremona, subscribed. John, bishop of Tortona [Terdona], subscribed. Adelbertus, bishop, subscribed. Otger, bishop, subscribed. Sichelinus, bishop of Florence, subscribed. Albericus, bishop, subscribed. Artingo, bishop of the Church of Ausonia, subscribed. Insinno, bishop of the Church of Laucanensis [Lavicanensis], subscribed. Ertemarius Ancias, bishop, subscribed. Julianus, bishop of Nocera, subscribed. Stephen, bishop of the Church of Cervia, subscribed. Atto, bishop of Senigallia, subscribed. Lupus, bishop of Spoleto, wrote [the subscription]. Lyndo, bishop of the Church of Chiusi, subscribed.

Given on the third day before the Nones of January by the hand of Wido, bishop of the Church of Silva Candida and librarian of the holy apostolic See; in the third year, by God’s favor, of the pontificate of Lord John, supreme pontiff and universal pope, the thirteenth of that name, in the most holy See of the apostle blessed Peter; while the most pious Lords Otto and his namesake son, crowned by God as great emperors, were reigning; in the sixth year of the Elder’s empire and the first of the Younger’s, in the month of January, in the aforesaid eleventh indiction.

(Place of the seal.)

## VIII. Privilege of John XIII for the Monastery of Déols in the Diocese of Bourges (968)

He grants a privilege to the monastery of Déols.

[According to D. Bouquet, *Collection*, vol. IX, p. 236.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the religious abbot Ramnulphus of the monastery of Déols, built in honor of the holy Mother Mary and the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and to his successors forever.

The care of the whole Church has been entrusted to apostolic governance. Therefore whoever, by divine dispensation, succeeds to the holy Roman See must necessarily, wherever possible, promote the welfare of that Church.

Accordingly, we decree that the aforesaid monastery, which Ebbo of pious memory built, shall be free from the domination of every person—whether king, bishop, or any of Ebbo’s sons, daughters, or relatives—just as it was sanctioned by our predecessor through the authority of a privilege. The monks shall possess without any contradiction all the goods which they now appear to have or which shall henceforth be bestowed there.

I likewise assign and confirm to that place the village of Vodillon, with its appurtenances, which was bestowed by Gerard, a nobleman. We also assign the chapel of Saint Germanus; the church of Saint Mary; likewise that of Saint Dionysius; the *masuilium* in honor of the holy Savior; the meadows in honor of Saint Bonitus; and finally the olive groves in honor of Saint Sulpitius. We also assign, after the departure of the Bretons, the chapel beside the castle of Déols which they constructed.

Likewise, the chapel of Saint Martin within Castrumfort; also the church in the district of Poitiers; the saltworks in the district of Alnis; and the allod of Lavariacum with Monte Futario, together with all the goods which they now have or which the same monks shall henceforth possess and which, as we have already said, belong to them. Let them claim these for themselves in such a way that they are subject to no one whatsoever except the Roman See, as is contained in the aforesaid testament of Ebbo.

With this in view, we confirm by our apostolic authority to the same monastery those possessions which are lawfully granted to it. Let them appoint as abbot, without anyone’s contradiction, whichever member of their community they shall elect by sounder counsel, living communally and according to the rule.

But if anyone should attempt to intrude by payment or empty glory, with the monks consenting—God forbid—we prohibit such a person by apostolic interdict as a thief and robber. Rather, we command that a person be elected by those to whom blessed Benedict granted authority in this matter, one who will strive to govern the household of the Lord well, live communally as has been said, and strive more to benefit the brothers, insofar as he can, than to rule them.

We also establish for the same monastery the church of Saint Lusor, which the same monks purchased from a nobleman named Simon, at a price paid, through a written charter, so that nothing further may be demanded from them except a census of ten solidi.

May all who assist the aforesaid monastery in increasing its possessions or religion deserve to have Christ the Lord, his holy Mother, and the blessed princes of the apostles as their helpers. But, on the other hand, whoever in rashness or audacity presumes to harm or usurp the monastery, the brothers, or any possessions belonging to them, we bind, by the apostolic power granted to us by God, with the bond of anathema until the day of judgment, unless they repent.

For those who observe these provisions, may the grace and peace of Christ be multiplied, and so forth.

Written by the hand of Theodore, notary of the holy Roman Church, in the month of January, in the eleventh indiction.

## IX. Bull of Pope John XIII to Adalbert, Archbishop of Magdeburg (968)

He establishes for him primacy among all the prelates of Germany and equal honor with the chief prelates of Gaul.

[Mansi, *Councils*, XIX, 5.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved brother in Christ, Adalbert, archbishop of the holy Church of Magdeburg: eternal salvation in the Lord.

If we fortify and adorn by the privilege of our authority those places which have been founded especially for the salvation of the people and the conversion of a nation to God, we have no doubt that this pertains to advancement and to the worship of divine religion.

Therefore, since by our authority and that of your fellow provincials we have decreed that the See of Magdeburg, over which by God’s authority you preside, is archiepiscopal, we have sanctioned that it be fortified by the privilege of the apostolic See regarding the order, strength, primacy, and equality which it ought henceforth to possess among the other Churches.

By the authority, therefore, of almighty God, of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and of ourselves, we wish that you and your successors forever, and your Church, should have primacy over all the Churches of the archbishops and bishops who are in Germany—in order of sitting, judging, confirming, subscribing, issuing sentences, and every ecclesiastical order.

For those who are in Gaul, namely the Churches of Mainz, Trier, and Cologne, we likewise confirm by this privilege equal honor and similar authority in all things.

Furthermore, following the custom of the Roman Church, we wish your Church to have twelve cardinal priests, seven deacons, and twenty-four cardinal subdeacons, who shall use sandals and *lisinae* [the liturgical garments or insignia are uncertain]. In addition, we grant those same priests and abbots of the church of Saint John the Baptist, built in the suburb of that city, permission to use tunics.

Except for these persons and the bishops, no one may in any way presume to celebrate Mass upon the altar dedicated in honor of blessed Maurice. We fortify and adorn this provision by the present privilege with special reverence, not out of pride but for the sanctity of the place.

Therefore, dearest brother, remembering wisely the Lord’s commandments, be vigilant in governing the people entrusted to you and in winning souls, so that you may offer our Redeemer the fruit of good works in which you can rejoice.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary of the holy apostolic See, in the month of October, in the twelfth indiction.

## X. Another Bull of the Same Pope to the Same Person (in the same year)

He grants him and his successors the consecration of all bishops between the Elbe and the Saale, and the right to the pallium.

[Mansi, *Councils*, XIX, 5.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our most beloved brother and fellow bishop Adalbert, archbishop of the holy Church of Magdeburg: eternal salvation in the Lord.

Your life and character have until now made you so suitable, dearest brother and fellow bishop, that we do not hesitate, as with a good steward, to entrust much to you and to commit even more.

Since, therefore, the authority of God first, and then of your people, your fellow provincials, and ourselves, has promoted you to the pastoral summit of your people; and since so great a population of the Slavs beyond the rivers Elbe and Saale, newly acquired for God, cannot be adequately cared for by only a few shepherds, I entrust to the judgment of your administration and discretion the manner in which you should rationally and carefully divide and distribute parishes among the bishops subject to your See.

By the protection of the present privilege I establish and confirm that this shall be done with the care, diligence, and judgment of our most serene spiritual son, the emperor Augustus, who is the founder and author of that same Church of yours.

Therefore, since it has been granted by the apostolic See, over whose Church I preside by God’s authority, that the bishops who have been or shall be established beyond the Elbe and Saale may in future be consecrated by the rulers of your Church, and that they in turn may consecrate the archbishops of that same Church of yours, according to whoever is in office at the time, who shall receive the pallium from our See according to the custom of the Roman Church—

I admonish and solemnly charge your affection, dearest brother, to be vigilant in spirit, lest through a gift or favor you appropriate any advantage for yourself; the clause concerning “any petition of persons in holy orders” is textually corrupt or uncertain. Rather, let that office be entrusted to one whom the seriousness of his character and the conduct of his past life commend.

We pray almighty God to surround you with his protection and to grant that you fulfill by your works the office of the priesthood which you have undertaken.

Issued by the hand of Stephen, notary and librarian of the holy Roman Church, in the month of October, in the established twelfth indiction.

## XI. Privilege of Pope John XIII for the Monastery of Arles (968)

[According to D. Bouquet, *Collection*, vol. IX, p. 178.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all the faithful of Christ, present and future: perpetual greeting in the Lord.

[Col. 0968A] If those things which accord with pious desires are always to be granted, how much more must those which are recognized as pertaining to the steadfastness of divine worship not be denied in any way. Therefore let the goodness and prudence of you all know that a God-fearing and illustrious count named Oliba, coming to Rome to pray before the most blessed apostles Peter and Paul’s most sacred bodies, requested from us that we decree the monastery called Arulas—built by his grandfather’s brother in honor of the Lord and of Mary, ever-virgin Mother of God, situated in the territory of the county of Roussillon, in a place called Vallis Asperi, beside the bank of the river Têt, which is also called by that common name—to remain under the perpetual immunity of the holy Fathers and under the protection of our holy apostolic see, [Col. 0968B] together with all its appurtenant properties and possessions.

Therefore, moved by the prayers of his humility, through this our apostolic and inviolable decree we establish that this monastery of the Mother of God, in its entirety and for its stability, must remain perpetually under the authority and protection of holy Mother Church. We confirm to it all the properties which lawfully and reasonably belong to it from the beginning and must belong to it until the end of the age: cells, churches, ornaments, sacred vessels and utensils; villages, houses, male slaves, female slaves, freedmen and affranchised persons; waters, together with the gardens (*verdigaria*) on both banks and their surrounding areas; lands and watermills with their headwaters and the aqueducts themselves; fisheries; and all cultivated and uncultivated places, [Col. 0968C] together with all usages, revenues, or tithes and tributes. We further proclaim that all these things, and whatever may legally be said and named, within their boundaries and limits, are to remain undisturbed and unharmed under the ownership of that sacred monastery and for the benefit of the regular abbot or the monks serving God there.

At no time shall any bishop, duke, count, or any person, great or small, have permission to take away or violently possess anything among all the things belonging to it or that ought henceforth to belong to it, or to inflict upon it any harassment or opposition. Rather, all its movable and immovable possessions in general and in their entirety shall remain safe and intact for the use and increase of that sacred monastery, [Col. 0968D] under the protection of our apostolic see in perpetuity, from the present twelfth indiction.

We also decree that if the abbot who shall be there at any time—God forbid—should depart from the regular purpose and institution of blessed Benedict, or should alienate the property of that monastery, the aforesaid Count Oliba, or his successors, shall have permission to expel that abbot and to restore to its proper ownership whatever he has alienated, and, once the truth of the matter has been established, to appoint in his place another abbot worthy of God.

By apostolic censure, under the solemn adjuration of divine judgment, we establish that what has been decreed by us is to be observed inviolably by all for all time. If anyone—which we do not believe—should presume, with reckless audacity, to oppose the tenor of this our [Col. 0969A] decree, let him know that, unless he repents, by the judgment of almighty God and of the aforesaid ever-virgin Mary, Mother of God, of the most blessed apostles Peter and Paul, of all the bishops, and by the authority of our humility, he is condemned with all the impious to everlasting fire and an unbreakable anathema. But whoever proves throughout to be its observer and guardian may obtain grace and mercy from the heavenly King and, with all his sins forgiven in the present life, attain eternal glory with the holy angels in the life to come.

Written by the hand of Leo, notary, regional officer, and scrinarius of the apostolic see, in the month of December, in the twelfth indiction. Farewell.

## XII. Privilege of Pope John XIII for the Monastery of Saint Michael of Cuxa. (Year 968)

[Marini, *Papiri diplomatichi* I, 52.]

[Col. 0969B]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, sends apostolic blessing and grace in perpetuity to our beloved son in Christ Warin, religious abbot of the sacred monastery of Saint Michael the Archangel and Saint Germanus, situated in the valley of Conflent and in the place called Cuxa, and through you to your successors, the regular abbots, and to the monks of that monastery.

Since the great care of solicitude presses upon us to keep watch over all the Churches of God, lest any of them should suffer loss through want in the future, we deem it worthy, out of regard for piety, to fortify places well ordered for the honor of almighty God by the authority of an apostolic privilege and to confirm them with all the property belonging to them. Therefore, because you requested from us, through the intervention of the praiseworthy and magnificent Count Oliba, that we reconfirm to you and to your successors, the regular abbots, the aforesaid monastery—which his brother, Count Xenofred of good memory, renewed, endowed, and enlarged for love of the heavenly homeland, gathering monks for the praise and service of the heavenly King and in honor of the aforesaid saints, namely the archangel Michael and the confessor Germanus—we, moved by your prayers and his, reconfirm, strengthen, and establish under continuous immunity and present protection that venerable monastery, situated on the bank of the River Llitera, [Col. 0969D] with all its boundaries and limits and all its movable and immovable property generally and in full belonging to it, for the use and support of the regular brothers now and in the future serving God there, just as it appears to have been confirmed or strengthened by our most holy pontifical predecessors and by the most Christian kings of the Franks.

First, the village of Cotolet and the village of Taurinyà, with the church of Saint Fructuosus and all its appurtenances. Likewise, the village called Cortis, and everything situated between these boundaries around the monastery: that is, on the eastern side, the boundary runs along the crest of the Serra, by which one proceeds to the pass of Claira; then to the mountain called Lacarias; from there it follows that mountain to the mountain called Categonis; then it descends southward along the Serra above the place called Miliarias and reaches the Cross above the village called Curtis. From there it extends to the rock or Cher of Clarint; then it proceeds along the crest of the Serra to the stream Merdarium and follows it to the river called Tecle. On the side of the northwest, that is, on the western front, it reaches the public road called the Two Sisters and follows that public road to the Llitera. Then, on the northern side, it extends beneath Saint Felix and reaches the allod of Saint Mary.

Likewise, elsewhere, the church of Saint Martin with the village of Claira, with its boundaries and appurtenances. Likewise, the village of Castellà with the two churches founded there, namely those of Saint Andrew and of blessed Mary ever-virgin, with their allod, tithes, first fruits, and all their furnishings. That village lies between the following boundaries: on one side, the boundary of Molig, or the place called Petrafita; on the other, the place called the Chest of Casalons; it proceeds through the Coma toward the River Têt; on the third side it has the farmsteads of Mengon. On the fourth side is the boundary of Canoa or Petrafita, and it reaches the River Têt; beyond that river, as much as Count Xenofred held on the day of his death; and the village of Torrent, with its boundaries, limits, and appurtenances, as the monastery itself appears to possess by written charter.

The entire village of Tarefage, and the allod of Molig, insofar as it belongs to that monastery. Likewise, whatever belongs to it of the allod of Mosedo, and whatever belongs to it of the allod of Arboussols and Planès, between the streams, and in the village of Mosset and the village of Felluns, according to their boundaries and limits.

Likewise, in the valley of Saurin, the church of Saint Michael with all its appurtenances. In the county of Fenouillèdes we confirm all the property belonging to that monastery; in the valley of Conflent, all its property with its boundaries and limits.

Likewise, in the county of Cerdanya, the village of Oruç, with its villages and hamlets and all their appurtenances; the allod of Anglès, with the Market itself and its boundaries and limits; the village of Llagona with the church of Saint Vincent and its boundaries and limits; the village of Bolvir with the church of Saint Thomas, its villages and hamlets, and all its limits; and the villages of Laren, Mazunculas, Talax, and Ozeja, with the church of Saint Stephen; Salton with the church of Saint Maurice; the parish of Saint Peter of Infurcato; the church of the Savior of Sponna with its tithes and first fruits; and the village of Vulcarca with its boundaries.

Aragolisa with its allod and the church of Saint James; Buluir with the church of Saint Cecilia and the Poio itself; the parish of Saint Thomas situated in Ventegiola, with its tithes and first fruits.

Likewise, all the property belonging to that monastery in the county of Cerdanya, with its boundaries; and in the county of Berga, the allod of Spongiola and Monte Negro; and all the allods belonging to that monastery; and in the valley of Conflent, the villages of Folionum, Setimdianum, Cornelianum, Vernetum, Cirisacum, Arrianum, Auger, and Henne; and in the village of Evulo, Juliulo, Campilias, Flazonum, Saorra, Foliolum, Torrendum, Pinum, Portinianum, and Mascaron; and all the other property of that venerable monastery situated in the valley of Conflent.

Likewise, in the county of Fenouillèdes, the church of Saint Cross with the castle and all its appurtenances. In the county of Roussillon, the allods of Petra Calcis, Saint Felix, Miliarium, Insula, Tunorium, the Valley of Ventosa, Corbaria, Nifiagum, Poium Vuscani, and the boundary of Vallis Asperi and the valley of Conflent; the allod of Vallis Magna with its boundaries and limits [sic].

In the county of Besalú, the allod of Centenys with its boundaries and limits, as well as those situated in other places. Likewise, in the county of Osona, the allod of Saliforas and another allod that belonged to Oddo.

All these things, therefore, whether they are called by these names or by others, and all property situated in whatever place, which can be said and named, which belongs to that monastery up to the present and which, through any acquisition, by written instruments or without written instruments, ought to belong to it until the end of the age, we grant in every respect to you, our aforesaid son Abbot Warin, and to your successors, and through this our protection we confirm them perpetually: lands, vineyards, fields, meadows, pastures, woods, churches, villages, houses, buildings, cultivated and uncultivated places, waters and watermills, [Col. 0971C] tithes, first fruits, and all usages and revenues, together with male and female slaves and male *aldiones* and female *aldeae* (persons of semi-free status), and everything that can be said and named.

Establishing by the authority of God and our own—and indeed formally declaring—that no king, no bishop, no duke, no count or viscount, and no person, great or small, may dare to inflict any violence or opposition upon you or your successors concerning all the property belonging to the monastery of Saint Michael and Saint Germanus listed above. Nor shall any of them have permission to harass your free or enslaved people without your consent or to compel them into service.

Rather, from now until the end of the age, that same place, with all that now belongs to it and ought henceforth to belong to it, shall remain quietly and peacefully under the authority of holy Roman Mother Church, whose jurisdiction it is, for regular and monastic tranquility, with the contradiction of all people entirely and everywhere removed.

If anyone—which we do not believe—should presume in any respect to oppose this our apostolic privilege, unless he repents completely, let him know that, by the authority of almighty God and of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and by our apostolic judgment, he is accursed, rejected, and anathematized, separated from the fellowship of Christ’s faithful and of the holy Church of God, condemned without end with all the impious, and burned in everlasting fire with Judas the betrayer.

But whoever strives to guard and diligently observe what has been decreed by us may deserve, through the intercession of our most merciful Lord and of us and all the saints, to obtain the grace of blessing and, joined to the angelic hosts, happily attain the everlasting joys of blessedness.

[Col. 0972B] Written by the hand of Stephen, notary, regional officer, and scrinarius of the holy apostolic see, in the month of December and in the twelfth indiction. Farewell. Nevertheless, by this act we do not wish any new right to be acquired by you or by that monastery, but only the ancient right to be preserved.—Given at Viterbo, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the third year.

## XII bis. Bull of Pope John XIII for the Ascetic House of Quedlinburg. (Year 969)

[Note: [Col. 0971D] The letter of Pope John which I now append was sent to me by the most distinguished man Bartholomeo Prospero Camellini of Reggio, now residing at Modena. He himself received it from the most distinguished Antonio Ulrico Eraht, who had extracted it from the principal archive at Brunswick, entrusted to his care. I felt obliged to disclose both their names, so that the public might know to whom thanks for this acquisition are chiefly due.

To tell the truth, however, there are several features in it which raise doubts about the authenticity of this document, since unusual formulas of John XIII occur in it, such as “nostrae,” and so forth, and “archibrothers,” as well as the other expressions occurring immediately at the beginning: “of body and mind,” and so forth. There are also some errors in the names of the bishops which may be or may have been those of a copyist. Finally, the indiction is plainly wrong here. Whatever the truth may be, I judged that this bull should be printed, leaving the judgment to learned readers. Nor do I presume, as though speaking from the tripod, to declare with certainty that this bull is forged, especially since the other things read here fit the age of John XIII sufficiently well. Mansi.]

[In Mansi, *Concilia* XVIII, 505.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, sends the fullness of heavenly grace and apostolic blessing to Mahetilda, incomparably praiseworthy on account of the nobility of body and mind, Augustan in generosity, venerable abbess of the monastery called Quedlinburg, and through her to all her successors and to the holy congregation of the handmaids of Christ dwelling there.

Since, through blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, whose office we exercise, though unworthy, we appear to possess throughout the world, by evangelical authority and the authentic authority of the holy Fathers, the rights of ecclesiastical power, we therefore trust that we can, without any Catholic resisting, specially administer all things that pertain to the praise of almighty God and orthodox religion.

Therefore we wish the whole body of Christ’s faithful to know how, through the intervention of our beloved and spiritual son, Lord Otto, ever-Augustus, your father, and of his most holy mother, Mahetilda Augusta, your most serene grandmother, we have received the aforesaid place of Quedlinburg, situated in Saxon territory and of which you appear to be in charge, under the jurisdiction and continuous protection of holy Roman Mother Church, over which we preside; with our archbrothers assembled in synod at Ravenna agreeing and consenting to this apostolic paternal decision, namely Peter of Ravenna, Rodaldus, patriarch of Aquileia, and the other bishops: Wido of Silva Candida, Benedict of Porto, Marinus of Sutri, Sicco of Velletri, John of Spoleto, Londoardus of Modena, Lutifridus of Pavia, Liutprand of Cremona, Hubert of Parma, and our other fellow bishops from Italy and beyond the Alps, fifty in number. Thus, from the present tenth day before the Kalends of May, it is specially known to have been established and placed forever under the patronage and protection of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and of his vicar, with everything belonging to it.

Therefore, by apostolic censure, we decree that the same monastery shall henceforth remain entirely free until the end of the age, by the authority of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has established the Church upon Peter. Through him we command and admonish, formally declaring, that no emperor, king, or duke, no bishop, and no person of whatever dignity or power, sacred or worldly, may dare to harass or disturb the abbesses of that place, or in any way alienate any of the property of that sacred monastery, or diminish what belongs to it.

Rather, let it remain quiet and undisturbed with all its possessions: male and female slaves, free persons and persons bound by tenure, [Col. 0973C] cultivated and uncultivated lands, and all property that can be said and named, which it now possesses and ought henceforth to possess by any transaction.

For the protection of you and your successors, we decree that you and those who succeed you in governing that holy place shall annually pay one pound of silver to our holy Roman Church, to be used for making lamps before the body of the aforesaid prince of the apostles. But if, through some difficulty in the course of the journey [lacuna], the same payment cannot be made each year, permission is granted for it to be accumulated and sent to the Roman Church at another time.

If anyone—which we scarcely believe—should attempt to act in any way against God by violating the tenor of this privilege, and should try to remove that monastery from the jurisdiction of the apostolic and Roman [Col. 0973D] Church, unless he repents, let him be bound by the chain of perpetual anathema and, by the authority of God and of his supreme key-bearer, and through the humility of us and all our pontifical successors, be joined forever to the devil with Judas, the betrayer of the Lord.

But whoever strives to be its observer and guardian may deserve to obtain forgiveness of all his sins and, joined with blessed Peter and the assemblies of the saints, attain joys without end.

Furthermore, we command that no abbess there shall ever be ordained or appointed by anyone except by the election, favor, and will of all the holy sisters who at the time are seen to be serving God there. Farewell.

Written by the hand of Stephen, scrinarius of the holy [Col. 0974A] Roman Church, in the month of April, in the sixteenth indiction. Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of May by the hand of Wido, bishop of the holy Church of Silva Candida and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the eleventh year—God being favorable—of the pontificate of the lord John, supreme pontiff and universal thirteenth provider of the holy Roman Church; in the sixth year of Otto, crowned by God, Augustus, governing the monarchy of the Roman Empire happily; in the sixteenth indiction.

## XIII. Privilege of Pope John XIII for the Church of Trier. (Year 969)

[In Hontheim, *Historia Trevirensis diplomatica*, vol. I, p. 305.]

[Col. 0974B]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, sends perpetual salvation in the Lord to our beloved brothers in Christ, all bishops, and to Catholic men of every dignity and order, present and future.

Although unworthy, nevertheless by the grace of divine favor and disposition we have assumed the most sacred see of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and the universal ministry throughout the whole world. It is therefore necessary that we continually exercise the most diligent care for all the Churches, lest their rights, established and confirmed inviolably by the authority of that same prince of the apostles and of his other venerable successors, should be diminished or perish in our time, but rather that, strengthened, they should suitably increase and prosper.

Therefore we wish your holiness and prudence all to know that when Theodoric, our most beloved brother and archbishop of the Church of Trier, came to Rome to pray at the thresholds of the holy apostles, we learned—as we had previously discovered by hearing, indeed by reading—that this same church, before the other churches of Gaul, received the beginning of the Christian religion and the first foundations of the Catholic faith through the evangelical teaching of the most holy men Eucharius, Valerius, and Maternus, and the others whom the aforesaid most blessed apostle Peter ordained and instructed in their time and also sent there to preach.

Therefore, with the counsel of the entire body of our apostolic see and by free consent, we have judged it worthy to reconfirm, strengthen, and restore in every way to the Church of Trier and to the aforesaid brother of ours, Theodoric, and through him to all his successors, the rights of the privileges which the holy Roman Mother Church authentically granted from the beginning until now to those saints and to their other successors, namely Agritius, Maximinus, Paulinus, Severus, illustrious and apostolic men, and which are also shown to have been destroyed by the ruin, fire, or some other disaster of the city.

By the force of this our apostolic privilege we decree that whenever a bishop, priest, deacon, subdeacon, or any ordinary legate of the apostolic and principal see is sent into Gaul or Germany for ecclesiastical business or for convening a synod, the bishop of Trier shall hold the first place among the other pontiffs after every ordinary legate of the apostolic see. If no envoy of the Roman Church is present, he shall likewise have precedence after the emperor or king in sitting, pronouncing judgment, and canonically promulgating synodal decisions, since he has rightly been constituted vicar of our apostolic see in those regions.

For it is not fitting that the bishop of that church should ever be regarded as inferior to the others, since the honor of that church in those regions was first established under the prince of the apostles.

In the same way we decree that all who dwell in its parishes, or who receive ordination and promotion to any ecclesiastical rank from its bishop, must canonically please, obey, and rightly submit to that mother Church and to its bishop. For the decree of Pope Clement appears to have taken the following precaution on this matter:

“If all the priests, deacons, subdeacons, and all the other clergy do not obey you bishops, and if all the rulers, both of higher and lower rank, and all the other peoples, tribes, and languages do not obey, they shall be excluded from the thresholds of the holy Church of God, the Lord saying: ‘Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever despises you despises me.’”

Among all these things which appear to belong to the aforesaid Church of Trier within and outside the city—that is, churches with all their appurtenances, and monasteries both of monks and of virgins, which by decrees or writings of kings or emperors, or by the authority of their founders, belong and ought to belong to it—and whatever that same church possesses or ought to possess anywhere and by any lawful title, we grant generally and specifically. Through the tenor of this our apostolic decree we restore them to the aforesaid Theodoric, our brother and fellow bishop, and to his successors, for the perpetual lordship and authority of the holy Church of Trier, valid from the present twelfth indiction until the end of the age.

If anyone should presume in any way to act against this, or attempt in any respect to violate what has been justly and canonically decreed by us, let him know that, by the authority of almighty God, of the aforesaid most blessed prince of the apostles, of all the saints, and then by our own authority, he is to be condemned and anathematized and assigned, with all the impious, to eternal punishments.

But those who faithfully strive to observe, guard, and fulfill this privilege of ours may deserve effectively to obtain from the Lord God, in the heavenly camps among the number of the elect, the grace of blessing and the fullness of mercy.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary, regional officer, and scrinarius of the holy apostolic see, in the month of January and in the twelfth indiction. Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of February by the hand of Sicco, bishop of the holy Church of N. [Blera], acting in the place of Guido, bishop and librarian of the holy apostolic see. In the fourth [another reading: third] year of the pontificate of the lord John, pontiff and universal Pope XIII, in the most sacred see of the apostle Peter; in the seventh year of the empire of the lord Otto the Great and the second of the younger Otto, and in the twelfth indiction.

[Note: [Col. 0975D] The seventh year of the empire of the lord Otto is corrected by Browerus to the eighth. That is indeed correct; nevertheless, stricter critics might thereby find an opening for attacking this charter on chronological grounds, just as the same error had provided material for the learned Eckhart to dispute, in his *Annotations on Schannat’s Diocese of Fulda*, no. 29, pp. 42 ff., against the bull of this same John XIII granted in the preceding year to the Church of Fulda concerning the abbatial primacy.

But who does not know that the years of the Ottos, both in Italy and in Germany, were sometimes incorrectly counted by notaries—so certainly that the republic of letters would suffer enormous loss if every charter had to be rejected as spurious whenever it reported the chronological notices of the Ottos incorrectly? Among others, Kettner observed this in his *Antiquities of Quedlinburg*, p. 697. After examining the entire archive while composing his history, he frankly confessed that he had labored in vain to reconcile the years of the Ottos, especially with the indictions.

Our document should be even further removed from any suspicion of fabrication because Leo IX testifies that it was shown to him in an unquestionable charter, which we shall refer to under the year 1049.]

## XIV. John XIII Grants Theodoric, Archbishop of Trier, the Use of the Pallium. (Year 969)

[In the Royal Archive at Berlin. From the papers of Pertz.]

## XV. The See of Benevento Is Honored with the Title of Archbishopric. (Year 969)

[Mansi, *Concilia* XIX, 19.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our most beloved Landulf, venerable and deservedly honorable bishop of the holy Church of Benevento and Siponto, and now, by the grant of our apostolic authority, archbishop.

[Col. 0976C] Since it is certain that ineffable rewards in the eternal kingdom are reserved for those who serve God, it is nevertheless necessary for us to bestow benefits upon them, so that through recompense they may be able to labor all the more abundantly in the praises of God.

And because we have learned that the Church of Benevento devotes itself to the exercise of God’s praises with great effort and pious religion, and that it has shown particular abundance of reverence toward the holy apostolic Roman Church—as was wholly evident when we formerly remained there—we ought therefore, out of the ardor of charity and zeal for divine worship, to exalt it among the other churches for the sake of honor and reverence.

And since it is a holy see where the body of blessed Bartholomew the apostle rests, it is fitting to adorn it with an increase of worship. For we have also undertaken the care of governance with a view to this, and, in order to offer diligent service to God and ringing praises of his power, we ought carefully to invite the devoted.

[Col. 0977A] Therefore, while we were presiding in the holy synod held before the confession of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June, with the four holy Gospels placed in the midst, in the presence of the lord Otto, most glorious emperor Augustus, and of Romano, our son, as well as many religious Romans, Italians, and westerners, and Catholic and most wise men of every order; at the gracious urging of the aforesaid most merciful lord emperor Augustus, together with the consent of the bishops and priests listed below and of all the clergy of the holy Roman Church who subscribed below, by whom [lacuna] it was desired to exalt the see of Benevento; with the intervention of Landulf, prince of the cities of Benevento and Capua, and of the margrave and duke of the duchies of Spoleto and Camerino, together with Landulf, his most excellent princely son, we have granted to you, aforesaid bishop, the use of the pallium for celebrating Mass alone, namely on these feasts:

on the Nativity of the Lord; the Epiphany; the Purification of holy Mary, Mother of God and Virgin; likewise the Annunciation of blessed Mary; Easter; the Ascension of the Lord; Pentecost; the feast of Saint John the Baptist; the feasts of the births of the blessed apostles; the Assumption of blessed Mary; likewise her Nativity; the dedication of the holy Church of your archbishopric; the day of your consecration; and the consecration of bishops.

We further grant you, together with it, the authority and honor of an archbishopric, so that your fraternity and your successors, within your diocese and in the places where they formerly existed, may always and forever consecrate bishops subject to your authority, namely those of Saint Agatha, Avellino, Quintodecimo, Ariano, Ascoli, Bibino, Vulturara, Larino, Telese, and Alife.

We have also added that you may use the pallium on the feasts of blessed Michael the archangel and the translation of blessed Bartholomew the apostle.

But the later rulers of your Church, after your death, shall receive the consecration of that archbishopric and the honor of the pallium from this holy and apostolic see, which, by God’s authority, I serve.

We likewise confirm to you and to your successors Siponto and the church of blessed Michael the archangel on Mount Gargano, and the town of Varano with its estates, villages, and all the appurtenances of its churches, just as they appear to have been possessed by concessions of privileges from our predecessors.

Furthermore, by apostolic censure, under the adjuration of divine judgment and by powerful and dreadful prohibitions of anathema, we decree that no person endowed with authority of any dignity, nor any person, great or small, may ever presume or dare in any way to destroy them. We decree with irrefragable right that the arrangements remain as they are, provided—as was said above—that your successors do not delay receiving from the holy Roman and apostolic see the consecration and use of the pallium according to the decree.

If anyone—which we do not desire—should presume with criminal audacity to oppose or destroy these provisions, or to inflict any loss or harassment, let him be bound by the chains of anathema and burned in the fire of eternal punishment with the devil and his most dreadful pomp and with Judas, the betrayer of our Lord Jesus Christ.

But whoever, with pious regard, proves to be an observer and guardian in all things of this apostolic institution, looking toward the worship of God, may abundantly obtain the grace of blessing from our most merciful Lord God and deserve to become a participant in eternal life. Amen.

Written by the hand of Stephen, scrinarius of the holy Roman Church, in the month of May, in the twelfth indiction.

I, John, thirteenth pope of the holy Catholic and apostolic Roman Church, have subscribed with my own hand to this privilege promulgated by us.

[Col. 0978B] + + Sign of the lord Otto, most pious emperor. Sico, s[lacuna] of the Church, consented to and subscribed this privilege. John, bishop of the Church of Galese. John, bishop of the Church of Anagni. Marinus, bishop of the holy Church of Sutri. Benedict, bishop of the holy Church of Terracina. Leo, bishop of the holy Church of Ostia. Benedict, bishop of the holy Church of Porto. Gregory, bishop of the holy Church of Albano. John, bishop of the holy Church of Salerno. John, humble bishop of the holy Church of Castro. John, bishop of the holy Church of Sarsina, consented and subscribed. [Col. 0978C] Stephen, bishop of the holy Church of Ficulle, consented. Constantine, bishop [lacuna]. Ignizzo, bishop of the Church of Florence. Hubert, bishop [lacuna], subscribed. Guifridus, bishop of the holy Church of Verdun. Sigulfus of the holy Church of Piacenza consented and subscribed. Liutprand, bishop, was present. Bozzo, bishop of the holy Church of Asti, consented. Abraham, bishop of the holy Church of Frising, consented. Raterius, bishop of the holy Church of Marsica, consented and subscribed. [Col. 0978D] Reginald, bishop of the holy Church of Rubilana, consented and subscribed. Alberic, bishop of the holy Church of Rieti, subscribed. Domninus, archpriest of the holy Roman Church, consented and subscribed. Crescentius, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church, consented and subscribed. Theophylact, priest of the holy Roman Church, consented and subscribed. Benedict, archdeacon of the holy Roman Church, consented. I, Boniface, humble deacon of the holy Roman Church, consented. Leo, deacon of the holy Roman Church, consented. John, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, consented.

Given on the seventh day before the Kalends of June by the hand of Guido, bishop of the holy Church of Silva Candida and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope John XIII, in the seventh year of the emperor Otto the Great and the second of the younger Otto, in the aforesaid twelfth indiction, in the year 969 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

## XVI. Privilege of Pope John XIII for the Monastery of Fulda. (Year 969)

[In Dronke, *Codex diplomaticus Fuldensis*, p. 330.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our most beloved son in Christ, Werinharius, the most religious abbot of the sacred monastery of Fulda, and through him to his successors in the abbacy forever.

[Col. 0979B] The desire which is shown to pertain to the purpose of religion and to the stability of holy places must, with God as its author, be fulfilled without any delay, so that thereby the strength of holy religion may be reinforced, the safety and security of those same holy places may be made firm, and for us also the most excellent reward of gain may be credited by God, the creator of all things, in the heavenly kingdoms.

Therefore, because the aforesaid abbot Werinharius, through the intervention of our most excellent and most devout emperor Augustus, Lord Otto, our spiritual son and defender of the holy Church, petitioned us that the venerable monastery over which he appears to preside—formerly built by the blessed bishop Boniface of holy memory in honor of God and our Lord and Savior, in the place called Boconia, beside the bank of the river Wultaha—might be adorned with the insignia of a privilege from the supreme apostolic see [Col. 0979C], and that, just as it has been placed under the authority of our holy Church, which by God’s will we serve, through the constitution of the most holy Pope Zachary and the decrees of our other venerable pontifical predecessors, so it might remain throughout perpetual ages and never be subjected to the jurisdictions of any other Church: therefore, favoring his pious desires, by this our authority we commit what is requested to worthy effect.

Accordingly, we prohibit every priest of any Church from exercising any authority or jurisdiction whatsoever in the aforesaid monastery, except the apostolic see. Thus, unless he has been invited by the abbot of the monastery, no one may presume in any way to celebrate the solemn offices of Mass there [Col. 0979D]. In this manner, in accordance with the fact that it stands subject to the apostolic see with the firmness of a privilege, it shall remain perpetually and securely endowed with its lands and possessions—universally, both those which it ought to claim for itself from the beginning and those which it now holds and possesses, as well as those which divine providence may in future wish to add to the right of this sacred monastery from the gifts, offerings, and tithes of any of Christ’s faithful—without opposition from any person, and shall enjoy them with perpetual security.

Moreover, out of our great love for the aforesaid most devout and most Christian Lord Otto, emperor Augustus, we specially decree that the same abbot of Fulda shall hold the first place among the abbots of Gaul or Germany wherever they assemble, and that he shall also remain, by our apostolic authority, the more esteemed and honorable archimandrite [Col. 0980A].

We also decree by the page of this our document that if any prelate of any Church, or any person endowed with whatever dignity, should attempt to violate or transgress the tenor of this privilege, which we confirm and reconfirm by the authority of the blessed prince of the apostles, whose office we hold, let him be anathema; let him incur the wrath of almighty God and be excluded from the assembly of all the saints. Nevertheless, the dignity of the aforesaid monastery, granted by us, shall remain forever inviolate, supported in all things by apostolic authority.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary and regional officer of the holy Roman Church, in the month of October and in the thirteenth indiction.

[Col. 0980B] Given on the sixth day before the Ides of November, by the hand of Wido, bishop and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the fourth year of the pontificate of our lord Pope John XIII, in the eighth year of the empire of our lord Otto Augustus the elder and the second of the younger, in the thirteenth indiction.

## XVII. Privilege of John XIII for the Monastery of Saint Vincent at Metz (970)

[In Pertz, *Monumenta Germaniae historica*, Scriptores, vol. IV, p. 471.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our most beloved son Theoderic, prelate of the holy Church of Metz.

[Col. 0980C] Since the duty of pastoral care compels us to proclaim abundantly whatever is recognized as pertaining to the stability of pious places while the praises of God are being recorded, and to confirm it by the judgment of apostolic institution in privileges and decrees, it is fitting that, through apostolic governance, we suitably order and unquestionably bring to a better condition those holy and venerable places which had long lain in ruins and lived in great want and poverty.

This is especially fitting where what is requested concerns not temporal advantage but the everlasting welfare of souls serving God: namely, that the venerable place which our most beloved son Theoderic has gathered together and joined into one, together with its own communities [Col. 0980D], which regularly keep sleepless vigils before God our Savior Jesus Christ with psalms, hymns, and prayers, protected from external disturbances, may continually perform the duties of pious service in the monastery of Saint Vincent.

Since it is established that your religious devotion has requested from us the apostolic confirmation of this privilege, on account of changes in temporal affairs and the various vicissitudes of human beings, we have decreed that the protection of Saint Vincent the martyr of Christ, with everything belonging to the same monastery, and the confirmation of you, your congregation, and your successors, shall be established forever. Thus, just as they are now arranged by you, they shall be preserved in the future until the end; and that congregation, remaining undisturbed as one body, may continually offer praises to God [Col. 0981A] and may be permitted to persevere continually in the devotion with which God has imbued its members.

The aforesaid place, established under one abbot, shall be undivided in honor of Saint Vincent, and the congregation shall remain undivided. No one shall be granted permission to flee the rigor of the rule to which he has devoted himself, wander here and there, or attempt to transfer himself to other monasteries; this we prohibit contrary to the rule under the bond of anathema.

Therefore, establishing and promulgating these things before God and before his terrible future judgment, by the page of this our apostolic privilege and decree we sanction, and by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, we decree and adjure both the future pontiffs of the apostolic see and all who shall exercise episcopal office, as well as every person, great or small, endowed with power of whatever dignity, that they shall in no way have permission to separate the frequently mentioned place of Saint Vincent, gathered into one and spiritually joined by the writing of apostolic authority, or to alienate anything from it, whatever may have been piously granted and bestowed upon that venerable place by the aforesaid Theoderic, our beloved son [Col. 0981B].

We command that the monastery of Saint Vincent be subject to the episcopal see of Christ’s protomartyr, Stephen, and that its abbot be elected under the authority of the bishop of that place. If the bishop is absent, the abbot may go to the episcopal see on feast days and celebrate Mass there wearing the dalmatic and sandals which we send to him.

[Col. 0981C] If meanwhile anyone—which we do not believe—should attempt with rash boldness to oppose the things piously and firmly established by this our authority through this privilege, or should presume to resist, remove, or alienate what has been established by the aforesaid Theoderic, our beloved son and prelate of Metz, for the praise of God and the stability of the aforesaid monastery, namely Saint Vincent, let him know that, by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, he is bound by the bond of anathema and will be burned with Judas, the betrayer of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the punishment of everlasting fire. Thus condemned, let him never be released from the bonds of the aforesaid anathema.

But whoever proves to be an observant guardian in all things out of pious regard, may obtain in many ways the grace of blessing [Col. 0981D] from our most merciful Lord God, become a participant in eternal life, and may this chain of blessed Peter open to him the gate of paradise. If, however, any bishop should wish to diminish anything from it, may this chain, as we have said, close the kingdoms of heaven to him.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary and regional officer of the holy Roman Church, in the month of September and in the fourteenth indiction. Farewell.

Given on the third day before the Kalends of October, by the hand of Wido, bishop and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the fifth year of the pontificate of our lord John, supreme pontiff and universal Pope XIII, presiding in the most holy see of the blessed apostle Peter; in the ninth year of the empire of Otto the elder and the third of the younger [Col. 0982A], and finally in the year 970 from the Incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ.

## XVIII. Lease of the City of Praeneste Made by John XIII to the Senator Lady Stephania, Subject to an Annual Rent of Ten Gold Solidi Payable to the Roman Church (970)

[Muratori, *Antiquitates Italicae*, III, 235.]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved daughter in the Lord, the most illustrious senator Stephania, and to your sons and grandsons.

Whenever things are expected to be granted by us which plainly accord with reason, it is fitting that we grant them willingly and offer suitable assistance to the desires of those who petition us [Col. 0982B]. Therefore, because you requested that we give, grant, and hand over to you, your sons, and your grandsons, by our apostolic authority, the city of Praeneste with all its appurtenances, together with every public payment and service belonging to the aforesaid city, within its new and ancient boundaries, namely:

the stream called Latus on the second side from Lavisana; on the third side, Monticellus of Maximus; on the fourth side, the Bridge of Cicala; on the fifth side, Aqua Alta; on the sixth side, the Valley of Caporatia; and on the seventh side, the mountain called Folianu.

Therefore, by this writing of our apostolic authority, we grant and hand it over, and from the present fourteenth indiction we confirm it, with all contradiction from our successors, the pontiffs, and from every person removed, so that you shall pay each year in our palace ten gold solidi, without postponement or difficulty [Col. 0982C]. You shall also unquestionably provide, without distinction, every improvement or defense which it requires; nor shall any delay on your part arise in paying the annual rent, but it shall be paid voluntarily to the officials of our holy Church at the proper time.

For if, God forbid, any delay on your part should arise concerning the aforesaid improvement or defense, or concerning payment of the annual rent, we decree that this our grant shall be invalid. After your death, however, the aforesaid city, together with all its improvements [Col. 0982D], shall in every respect return to the right of our holy Church.

Farewell.

Written by the hand of Stephen, notary of the holy Roman Church, in the month of November, in the fourteenth indiction.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January, by the hand of Wido, bishop and librarian of the holy apostolic see, in the sixth year of the pontificate of our most holy lord Pope John XIII, in the ninth year of the empire of our lords, the emperors Otto Augustus the elder and his son the younger in his third year, in the aforesaid fourteenth indiction.

## XIX. Letter of John XIII to the Bishops of Gaul: He Raises the Church of Ausona to Archiepiscopal Status (970)

[Col. 0983A]

John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all our most beloved brothers in Christ residing in the regions of Gaul, the most beloved and most reverend archbishops and bishops: apostolic blessing and perpetual salvation in Christ.

We wish your affection and fraternity to know how Borellus, an honorable and praiseworthy count, came to the thresholds of the apostles Peter and Paul for the sake of his prayer and redemption. Prostrate at our feet, he tearfully complained that we should subject the archbishopric of Tarragona—which [Col. 0983B] had formerly been the head of those regions—to the Church of Ausona, because, by reason of deserved sins, the aforesaid city of Tarragona had already been captured by the Saracens and deprived of its shepherd, and until now had been unable to find any opportunity for recovery or habitation.

For this reason, following the authority of my predecessors, we now and forever will, establish, strengthen, and confirm that the Church of Ausona shall hold the power and primacy of the Church of Tarragona, [lacuna] should flee to the Church of Ausona; and whenever any one of them departs from this life, his successor shall succeed and be consecrated by the archbishop of Ausona, who has been confirmed by our apostolic see.

Therefore, because we do not wish to confirm this privilege of ours without the authority of the holy Fathers, above all and before everything we produce and set forth the instruments and documents of the most blessed and eminent Pope Gregory, where he says to Benenatus, bishop of the Church of Musitana:

> “Both the character of the times and the proximity of the places invite us to unite the Churches of Cuma and Musitana, since they are separated from one another by no great distance, and, because of the sins of the people, there is not such a multitude of inhabitants that they ought to have separate priests, as formerly. Therefore, since the priest of the fortress of Cuma has completed the course of this life, know that by the page of our present authority we have placed both Churches under you and entrusted them to you, and know that you are the proper bishop of both Churches [Col. 0983D]. Accordingly, whatever you judge should be ordered and arranged concerning their property, the ordination of their clergy, or their advancement, in accordance with the statutes of the canons, you shall have free authority to arrange as their true priest, with the consent and permission of our authority.”

Likewise, to Bishop Willitranus, and to the bishop of Fundi and that of Squalita, he writes in all things as follows:

> “The character of the times advises that episcopal sees, formerly established in particular cities, should be transferred to other places of that diocese which we consider safer, so that the inhabitants may now live there and barbarian danger may more easily be avoided.”

Since it would be lengthy to recount what and how many documents have consequently been issued by the holy teachers [Col. 0984A], we have taken care to abbreviate our privilege as best we know and can. With God’s favor, we have decreed that Otto, a venerable man and recently made bishop, shall henceforth and in the future preside as archbishop over the same Church of Ausona [Note: [Col. 0983D] Peter de Marca asserts in *Marca Hispanica*, book IV, p. 403, that this decree had no effect because it was issued without the hearing of the archbishop of Narbonne. Martène.] Thus, none of our pontifical successors shall dare to disturb our brother Otto, the archbishop, in anything written or recorded above, or diminish anything from it, but shall rather preserve him and his successors peacefully and securely.

For if, God forbid, any person of whatever dignity should wish, for any reason, to violate or diminish this our privilege in any of the matters written above, let him know that, by the authority of God and of the apostles Peter and Paul, princes of the apostles—although we are unworthy to exercise their vicariate—we declare him alienated from the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ and separated, together with the wicked and transgressors, from the bosom of the holy Church [Col. 0984B].

But whoever proves to be a guardian and observer in all things out of pious regard, may he deserve to obtain the grace of blessing and mercy from our most merciful Lord God.

Written by the hand of Gregory, notary, secretary, and notary of the holy Roman Church, in the month of January, in the fourteenth indiction. Farewell.

## XX. Letter of Pope John XIII to Guisadus of Urgell, Peter of Barcelona, and Others (971)

He declares that he has joined the Church of Tarragona to that of Ausona, consecrated Atto as archbishop, and bestowed the pallium upon him. He urges them to obey him.

[In Flórez, *España Sagrada*, 3, XXVIII, 96.]
